Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise overview and attached a visual processing map and an evidence checklist for your security team (redwood-data-processing-map-2027-01.pdf, acme-evidence-checklist.xlsx). High-level answers below; see attachments for detail and subprocessor contact points.

1) Regions & routing
- Default hosted processing: requests from US customers are processed in our primary US region (us-west-2). For EU customers we use eu-west-1. ACME's tenant will be provisioned in the US by default.
- Cross-border routing: Redwood does not route US customer request payloads through EU data centers under normal operations. There are two controlled exceptions: manual failover (on-call engineers initiating cross-region recovery) and optional customer-configured routing for multi-region redundancy. Both are logged and require customer consent for persistent cross-region storage.

2) Subprocessors that may handle derived telemetry or logs
- Core compute: our managed GPU fleet (Redwood Compute Ops) — in-house and operated by Redwood.
- Cloud storage: object storage for logs and optional long-term artifacts is provided by our cloud provider partners (AWS S3 in configured region).
- Observability/analytics: Datadog (metrics/traces) and an internal analytics service (redact-first ingest).
- Auth/KMS: KMS provided by customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (optional) or Redwood-managed KMS if not supplied.

3) Deletion & retention flow
- Short-term request data: request payloads and ephemeral KV caches are ephemeral and deleted from serving nodes within 24 hours unless flagged for troubleshooting.
- Persistent logs/artifacts: retention defaults are 90 days for non-production/logging buckets. Customer tenants can configure shorter retention; we support configurable retention down to 0 days for logs.
- Tenant deletion: We support a "tenant purge" workflow — on a verified deletion request (API + manager approval) we: 1) disable new writes to tenant storage, 2) remove persistent artifacts from object storage, 3) purge tenant metadata from our orchestration DB, and 4) expire any KV cache snapshots. The process is recorded in an audit trail and an evidence bundle is generated (we can deliver on request).

We can also support Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) if ACME requires zero cloud subprocessors.

I've looped in Aditya (security) and Marissa (privacy) to provide the subprocessor inventory and SOC2 / audit evidence references.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

Jordan — apologies for the short delay. Attached is an updated evidence checklist with the signed purge attestation template and the expanded subprocessor inventory (see acme-evidence-checklist.xlsx). Quick answers inline below and in the attachment: 

1) Purge SLA & attestation
- We can commit to the 7-day completion SLA for the tenant purge on Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private agreements. For Hosted customers we provide the attestation and evidence bundle within 72 hours by default; contractual 7-day SLA is available with an enterprise addendum. A signed attestation PDF will be generated upon completion.

2) Observability traces and tenant boundary
- Observability traces (metrics/traces) are ingested into a tenant-scoped observability project and are logically separated. For hosted customers traces are stored in our provider's regional account scoped to the tenant and retention follows the tenant's configured policy. Traces do not flow to a global analytics pool. We redact prompt content before any external trace/analytics export.

3) Failover & cross-region
- Cross-region failover is strictly controlled: it requires a documented incident declaration, approval from the on-call SRE leader, and recorded customer notification unless you have explicitly agreed to automated cross-region failover in your config. You can opt out of automated or manual cross-region recovery for your tenant; we will document that in the security addendum.

Next steps: 1) Tessa, I'll hand the signed attestation template and the inventory back to you; 2) Jordan, if ACME wants Dedicated capacity or a Private deployment to avoid cloud subprocessors in production, we should schedule a short technical scoping call this week.

Regards,
